title: Autonomous routing backoff & tier-fallback policy for region and model variants
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement an autonomous backoff and fallback policy that protects customer SLAs by automatically routing traffic away from strained capacity (region or tier) and selecting fallback model variants. This ticket defines thresholds (429s, timeouts, error-rate), circuit-breaker state transitions, and the rules for selecting fallback models (smaller/quantized or regional replicas). The policy must be per-customer and per-route configurable, support canary rollouts, and include observability hooks and traces for debugging decisions.
implementation_notes:
1) Introduce an RT-based monitoring agent that computes sliding-window metrics per (route, region, model, tier) including p95 latency, 429 rate, 5xx rate, and GPU queue length.
2) Implement a policy engine with three modes: observe-only, soft-fallback, hard-open.
3) Soft-fallback: route 10% of traffic to fallback model when transient degradation meets soft thresholds.
4) Hard-open (circuit open): stop routing to primary after sustained threshold violation, route to fallback pool or alternative region.
5) Add hysteresis and cooldown: exponential backoff windows and minimum open duration to avoid oscillation.
6) Expose config via routing policy API and Console UI.
7) Add feature flags to enable canary (percent-based) and simulate mode for A/B testing.
design_decisions:
- Use sliding-window aggregation (60s window, 10s step) to balance sensitivity vs noise.
- Two-tier triggers: soft (early mitigation) and hard (guaranteed fallover). Soft-fallback reduces upstream impact while preserving primary preference.
- Circuit breaker states: CLOSED -> SOFT-OPEN -> OPEN -> HALF-OPEN -> CLOSED. SOFT-OPEN routes a configurable fraction to fallback while continuing monitoring.
- For fallback model selection prefer same-architecture quantized variants when available to limit quality regressions; fall back to regional replica only when model variant is unavailable or quality delta is unacceptable.
- Prioritize routing to Dedicated capacity for customers with reserved capacity before spilling to hosted fallbacks.
- Keep policy decisions tenant-scoped to avoid noisy-neighbor cross-customer effects.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed for metric collectors; prototype computes 60s sliding windows for p95/429/5xx per-model and per-region.
2026-02-20: Policy engine V0 implemented (closed/open logic) and wired into routing layer; added simulation mode for dry-run analysis.
2026-03-03: Integration tests added; found oscillation on short outages — implemented exponential cooldown and min-open duration (30s).
2026-03-12: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for internal test tenants; dashboards created, initial metrics look stable.
review_comments: PM (Priya Nair): Ensure Console exposes the fallback quality delta estimate and monthly cost delta before enabling automatic fallback for enterprise customers.
Design (Liam O'Connor): Add an explanatory tooltip in Console describing difference between soft-fallback and open-circuit states.
SRE (Nora Patel): Recommend adding GPU queue depth and host OOM rate as secondary signals to avoid routing on spurious 429 storms caused by rate limiting upstream.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine supports SOFT-OPEN and OPEN transitions with configurable thresholds.
Per-tenant and per-route overrides available and honored by the routing layer.
Canary rollout mechanism implemented (percent-based) and simulation mode available.
Dashboards show decision traces and key metrics; alert runbook updated.
Automated tests cover threshold edge-cases and state transitions; no regression on baseline latency for non-canary traffic.
test_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions, integration tests for policy-enforced routing, chaos tests simulating 429 spikes and region network partitions, and synthetic load tests to verify cooldown behavior. Run canary on internal orgs and two beta customers for 72 hours with intensive monitoring for quality drift.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated and off by default. 2) Enable simulation mode for 10% traffic for 48h. 3) Canary: 5% of production traffic for internal orgs, monitor 24h. 4) Expand to 20% and enable soft-fallback for selected customers. 5) After stable metrics for 7 days, enable for all tenants with default conservative thresholds.
Rollback: flip feature flag off; routing returns to previous deterministic path.
metrics_to_monitor: fallback traffic percentage and quality delta (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-sim)
example_trigger_configs: soft_fallback: { window_s: 60, p95_ms > 1500 AND error_rate_429_plus_5xx > 0.02 => fallback_pct: 0.10 }
hard_open: { window_s: 300, 429_rate > 0.05 OR (error_rate_5xx > 0.03 AND p95_ms > 3000) => open_duration_s: 120 }
estimated_risk: medium - risk of quality regressions when routing to smaller/quantized fallbacks; mitigated by conservative default fallback percentages, quality delta gating, and per-tenant opt-out.
next_steps: Finish Console UI for policy editing and per-tenant overrides (PRD linked).
Add GPU queue depth as a secondary signal to the policy agent (depend on ENG-22001).
Schedule canary with two beta customers next week and collect quality regression reports.
Draft customer-facing communication and updated runbooks for support teams.
